discovery: Quantum computation and quantum simulation with trapped ions: the theoretical blueprint and its experimental realization

nominees.name: Juan Ignacio Cirac
nominees.affiliation: Max Planck Institute of Quantum Optics, Garching, Germany

nominees.name: Peter Zoller
nominees.affiliation: University of Innsbruck and IQOQI, Austrian Academy of Sciences, Austria

nominees.name: Rainer Blatt
nominees.affiliation: University of Innsbruck and IQOQI, Austrian Academy of Sciences, Austria

subfield: Atomic, molecular and optical physics / quantum information
motivation: In 1995 Cirac and Zoller showed that cold ions in a trap, coupled through shared motion and addressed by laser light, could implement a universal quantum computer. This was the first concrete, physically realistic architecture for quantum logic. It turned quantum computation from an abstract idea into a laboratory programme, and it set the template for engineering controlled interactions in many later platforms. Blatt and his Innsbruck team carried this programme out with great precision: they demonstrated the Cirac-Zoller gate, deterministic teleportation, multi-qubit entanglement, quantum error-correction primitives and digital and analog quantum simulation. Cirac and Zoller went on to found the modern field of quantum simulation with cold atoms. Together these contributions created a new discipline of precision quantum control, now adopted by groups and companies worldwide. They complement, rather than repeat, the 2012 and 2025 prizes, and they mark the essential step from controlling single quantum systems to programmable quantum many-body devices.
